title: Propose / diff / apply workflow
goal: AI mutates the tree only through staged CLI proposals; user reviews diffs and explicitly applies or rejects before any live yaml changes.
out: concurrent pending proposals on root and fragments

claims.text: `propose` writes only to `*.proposed` (root: `nodes.yaml.proposed`; fragment: `fragments/foo.yaml.proposed`) and prints a unified diff — live yaml is untouched until `apply`
`apply` copies staged content into the live target and deletes `*.proposed`; `reject` deletes `*.proposed` without touching the live file
Only one pending proposal per project at a time — if root or any fragment is staged, a new `propose` fails and lists every pending target with pending/apply/reject commands
`apply` and `reject` require the same `--fragment` flag as `propose`; applying the wrong target prints which fragment/root is actually pending
claims.rationale: Clear error when user mismatches target

claims.text: `pending <project> [--fragment …]` reprints the staged diff against the current live tree for that target
`show <project>` lists every pending target (root and fragments) with the matching pending/apply/reject commands
Agent mode: `propose … --no-prompt` stages and prints pending/apply/reject commands; non-interactive stdin without `--no-prompt` also stages but tells user to finish in terminal (no fake y/n)
No-op proposals (`No changes.`) exit without creating `*.proposed`
Invalid operations (unknown op, bad JSON in `set-data`, missing batch payload) fail before staging any `*.proposed`
claims.rationale: Errors never leave partial pending state

claims.text: `propose <project> batch --file batch.json --no-prompt` applies all ops atomically in one staged diff via `apply_batch`
claims.rationale: Multi-step tree edits stay one review gate

claims.text: project-tree SKILL.md documents: show → propose --no-prompt → pending/apply/reject with matching --fragment, one pending per project, batch support
AI agents never edit `nodes.yaml`, `fragments/*.yaml`, or `*.proposed` directly — all mutations go through `project_tree.py propose`
claims.rationale: Enforced by skill, not code — user catches violations in review
